_doc: Freeze finished code at the source level.
Do not list paths only. A path with no reason gets unlocked by the next
person who needs it. What makes this work is what_breaks: the person
unlocking has to know what they are risking.
To unlock, the commit message needs three lines:
UNFREEZE: <path or label> - why this has to change now
UNFREEZE-IMPACT: what breaks, and how, if this is wrong
UNFREEZE-ROLLBACK: how to undo it, with the command if possible
If you cannot write the impact and the rollback, you are not ready to
unlock it. That judgment falls out of the three lines by itself.

frozen.label: Billing
frozen.reason: Finished and in production. Not on any roadmap.
frozen.what_breaks: Wrong math still renders a normal screen. Only the amount changes.
before_you_touch: Partial refunds live in refund.py, not here.
Failure rolls the whole transaction back. Do not weaken that.
Currency rounding is decided once, at the boundary. Not per call site.

frozen.label: Auth token issuance
frozen.reason: Security-critical and settled. Every change here needs review.
frozen.what_breaks: Sessions stay valid past expiry, or everyone gets logged out.
before_you_touch: Clock skew tolerance is deliberate. Do not tighten it without data.
Unknown algorithm means refuse, not fall back.

_note_not_frozen: Paths deliberately left out because the roadmap touches them soon.
If the freeze covers everything, the gate becomes the boy who cried wolf,
and then real violations get ignored too. Leave planned work open.
